_ruling: OWNER, 2026-09-01, Option A: a site enters this field only if it exists AT 3956. The alternative - record every place ever named on a world with an era note - was declined because BESPIN'S ENTRY ALREADY EXCLUDES CLOUD CITY IN PROSE, and a field admitting it anyway gives the project two answers to one question.
_consumed_by: LOOT-01 7c (PT-912). A named site takes 5's explicit override route; 4 is unchanged elsewhere on that world; world danger still caps both. THE SITE MOVES THE WORLD FROM 'GENERATED' TO 'AUTHORED, HERE'. It does not raise a tier.
_tests: NAMED AND VISITABLE, NOT IMPORTANT - Main, TO-ATLAS-19. Dellalt's decoy vaults qualify because a party can walk into them, not because Xim's treasure matters.
AT 3956 - owner ruling. Cloud City is c.400 BBY and does not enter.
ON THIS WORLD, NOT MENTIONED BY IT - this Atlas cross-references constantly by design. Urkupp's entry names the Jedi Temple on Coruscant; that is Coruscant's site.
INELIGIBLE WORLDS STILL COUNT - Tython has no homeworld menu and a party can still land on it.
_method: HAND-CURATED. A regex generated candidates; every entry below was judged by reading the sentence it came from. sweep_sites.py is marked STOPPED and records why: one case-sensitivity flag moved its output from 73 to 1,069, which is the instrument deciding the answer.

Korriban: the Valley of the Dark Lords
Rafa: the ruins of the ancient Sharu
Recopia: the Seyugi Dervish fortress at Mallif Cove

Each names a place that belongs to another world's entry - the Pits of Plooma quoted by five Veragi-block worlds, Belsavis's prison quoted by Dathomir, House Pelagia's library quoted by Praesitlyn and Ashas Ree, Kuat's shipyards quoted by Ruan and Illodia. THIS ATLAS CROSS-REFERENCES BY DESIGN and a matcher cannot tell a site ON a world from a site MENTIONED BY one.
